findings.description: The main-tree protection compares only git status entries, which do not capture file contents. If a tracked file is already modified before the probe, the probe can overwrite it and leave exactly the same status entry. The helper then exits successfully despite changing the main tree.
findings.failure_mode: A probe overwrites existing uncommitted work in an already-dirty file; the before/after status strings remain identical, so the ticket incorrectly passes and the overwritten contents are lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Fingerprint file contents before and after the probe, including existing dirty and untracked files, and fail when any fingerprint changes. Include ignored contents covered by the unchanged-tree guarantee.

findings.cross_file_justification: chart-researcher.md grants an unrestricted Write tool to a subagent that ingests untrusted WebFetch content; op_research_end in chart-ticket.sh is the only mechanical enforcement of the 'write exactly one file' rule, so a gap in its diff is a gap in the sandbox.
findings.description: The scope check compares two `git status --porcelain` listings and flags only lines that are new in the second listing (comm -13). A file whose status line is identical before and after is invisible: any tracked file already ` M` at dispatch time, or any untracked file already `??`, can be overwritten by the researcher without producing a new line. At the moment research-begin runs, `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` and `grimoires/loa/maps/<slug>.md` are almost always dirty, because op_ticket just wrote the open ledger row and the session is editing the map doc. A prompt-injected researcher (the agent file explicitly anticipates instruction-like text in fetched pages) can therefore append a `decided`/`operator:*` row to the ledger or rewrite the map doc, and research-end reports success. The awk filter also whitelists the whole `grimoires/loa/research/` directory, so overwriting other tickets' reports (which op_handoff later inlines) is likewise allowed. The `-newer` mtime check that would catch these is applied only to `.run` and `.beads`.
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted web content steers the researcher into writing the decision ledger or map doc; the scope check passes; the forged row is later treated as settled context by /plan-and-analyze and can unlock the FR-1.1 spike-branch deletion path in block-destructive-bash.sh.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot content, not status lines: in research-begin record `git -C ROOT status --porcelain` plus a content hash of the working tree (e.g. `git add -A --intent-to-add` is too invasive; instead hash `git ls-files -mo --exclude-standard -z | xargs -0 sha256sum`, or compare `git diff | sha256sum` and `git diff --cached | sha256sum`), and in research-end also run `find "$ROOT" -type f -newer "$m" -not -path '*/.git/*'` over the whole tree, excluding only the single expected report path (not the whole research/ directory). Fail if anything else changed.

findings.description: The probe's main-tree verdict has the same blind spot as DISS-001: it compares two porcelain listings as whole strings, so a probe that rewrites a file that was already modified or already untracked before the run is not detected. In addition, the throwaway worktree shares the main repo's object store and refs, so a probe can `git branch -f`, `git tag`, `git update-ref`, `git stash` or `git push` against the main repository without `git status` of the main tree changing at all. The header promises 'exits 1 when the main tree's status changed', which is narrower than 'never writes App-Zone code in the main tree'.
findings.failure_mode: An unblock probe silently alters already-dirty files or moves branch refs in the main repository and the helper exits 0, so the ticket records a clean probe.
findings.suggested_fix: Record and compare `git for-each-ref` output and a content hash of modified/untracked files alongside the porcelain listing; document the shared-refs limitation in the header if it is accepted.

findings.description: The new exemption lets `git branch -D spike/<slug>` through solely because a tracked YAML file says the verdict is decided. It never checks that the spike was actually pushed (SP-1 describes the spike as 'pushed as the pointer for a decision'), so a spike whose push failed or was never run is deleted along with the only copy of the prototype the DEC row points at. The gate also trusts `by: operator:*` text in a file the agent can edit with any text tool, so the ledger becomes a writable bypass of a hook whose job is to catch exactly that class of mistake.
findings.failure_mode: Operator decides the verdict, agent runs `git branch -D spike/x` before pushing (or after a rejected push); the hook allows it and the prototype commits become unreachable.
findings.suggested_fix: Additionally require `git rev-parse -q --verify refs/remotes/origin/spike/<slug>` to exist and to equal (or contain) the local branch tip before returning 0; keep the block otherwise.

findings.description: create-sprint-task.sh (same diff) documents that older br releases emit labels as `{name}` objects and handles both shapes. chart-frontier.sh's label filter does `tostring` on each label and checks `startswith("decision:")`; for an object label that yields the JSON text `{"name":...}`, which never starts with `decision:`, so every ticket fails the exactly-one-label test and the frontier is silently empty (exit 0, no output). The two scripts also disagree on the type field (`.issue_type // .type` here, `.issue_type` only in get-ready-work.sh).
findings.failure_mode: On a br version that emits object labels, `/chart <slug>` reports an empty frontier for a map that has open tickets, and the session may wrongly conclude it should hand off or close the map.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise labels the same way as create-sprint-task.sh: `[(.labels // [])[] | if type == "object" then (.name // "") else tostring end]` before the `startswith` test, and share the type accessor between the two scripts.
